notes:
Summary: Crestpoint CX Labs (large telco contact center org) evaluating Redwood for expanding existing automation stack into 24/7 contact-center workloads. They already run a combination of rules + small models for IVR and FAQ but want a platform to scale agent-assist, ticket summarization, and safe tool-calling under heavy spikes.

Key quotes / asks:
- "We need sub-400ms p95 for agent assist pipelines in our primary queues."
- "Public endpoints not allowed for any PII flows; VPC or private deployment required."
- "Target cost per resolved ticket < $0.35 — show how batching + caching helps."

Workload details / constraints:
- Primary workloads: live agent assist (real-time suggestions), transcript summarization for ticket creation, outbound message drafting, and automated tool-calls into CRM/OMS via safe function calls.
- Traffic shape: baseline ~4k concurrent chats; peak holiday spikes up to ~12k concurrent sessions for a 6-hour window. Need graceful degradation and fallbacks.
- Latency SLO: p95 <400ms for suggestions; p99 <1s preferable for short assistant actions.
- Throughput: sustained token throughput during spikes ~200k tokens/minute; POC tested up to 300k tokens/minute.
- Model preference: hybrid approach — lightweight local quantized models for hot-path suggestions + higher-capacity hosted models for long-form summarization and escalation. Open to Redwood recommendations and quantization profiles.

Security & compliance notes:
- Must pass internal security questionnaire (SOC2 + ISO27001 required). Crestpoint will require KMS/HSM integration and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. Data residency: EU for EU region queues; NA for US queues.

POC results (interim):
- Agent-assist accuracy: 72% useful suggestion rate in first 2 weeks (goal 85%).
- Spike test: 18% increase in latency at peak; caching + batch tuning reduced that to 6% in follow-up run (logs attached in Drive).
- Integration: Zendesk + Genesys API adapters work; need production-ready retry/backoff for tool-calling.

Decision-makers & stakeholders:
- Primary sponsor: Clara Jensen, Dir. Contact Center Automation (Exec Sponsor on POC calls)
- Procurement lead: Marcus Holt, Vendor Sourcing
- Security reviewer: Arun Patel, InfoSec

Next steps / asks for Redwood team:
- Deliver SOW draft with dedicated pool sizing options and burst capacity plan by 2026-03-10.
notes_short: Expanding POC to production contact-center workloads. VPC-only, SOC2 + KMS required. Spike resiliency and cost-per-ticket targets are the main blockers. POC showed promising caching wins but legal/security and KMS schedule remain blockers.
